Iran's rial has hit a record low, Tehran calls the US 'desperate', vows not a single drop of oil will leave the Gulf, threatens to seize vessels violating Strait of Hormuz transit rules, and warns that support for the sanctions will be treated as an act of war. Analysts remain uncertain whether the measures will effectively target China, Iran's largest trading partner. Trump also imposed 50% tariffs on Canada, prompting PM Mark Carney to vow to match the fees dollar for dollar, though Trump has signaled he wants Canada back at the trade-talks table.

PM Mark Carney suspended talks, saying last-minute US changes to the proposed deal were 'unfair, uneconomic' and questioned the reliability of any agreement, declaring Canada now 'at war' with the US over trade, and pledged dollar-for-dollar retaliatory tariffs on sectors including dairy, steel, household appliances, farming equipment, electronics and pulp and paper, set to take effect September 8. US Trade Representative Jamieson Greer said Canada had declined a deal, calling it a 'missed opportunity' and blaming Ottawa for wanting more. The Canadian dollar has slid as markets brace for a prolonged trade war, with Carney's government reportedly seeing little chance of resuming talks before the US midterm elections.

Burnham has directly challenged Putin over the war's origins, asking 'Who started the fire?', amid a Kremlin warning that the UK is now 'participating in this war'. Backbenchers have warned Burnham against calling a snap general election. Meanwhile, Zelenskyy says Russia plans to draft 300,000 more troops, has warned on the prospect of wartime elections, and declared in a defiant independence day speech that Ukraine wants peace but will not give in to Russia at any price, as Ukrainian drones struck three major Russian retail hubs near Moscow and attempted to strike a military cosmodrome. Moscow has since struck a cargo ship in the Black Sea after Zelenskyy called for talks to halt attacks, with Kyiv vowing to bolster regional air defences amid a renewed Black Sea blockade squeezing Ukraine's grain exports and farmers. Separately, the first British national is reported to have been killed fighting for Russia in a drone attack, and Burnham has signalled openness to cut-price tuition fees for EU students as part of a planned EU 'reset' summit. A key Ukraine ally was notably absent from the Kyiv gathering.
